name: Gayatri Rubbers and Chemicals Ltd
tagline: Micro-cap reclaimed-rubber and rubber-chemicals manufacturer with strong headline metrics (39.5% ROCE, 31% revenue growth, near-zero debt) riding India's tyre-recycling/EPR push, but on a tiny base with a largely commodity moat.
business_overview: Gayatri Rubbers and Chemicals Ltd (NSE: GRCL) manufactures reclaimed rubber, rubber products, rubber by-products and rubber chemicals from rubber scrap (largely end-of-life tyres), selling into tyre and rubber-goods manufacturers as a cost-effective substitute for virgin rubber. Entity confirmed via screener.in (ticker GRCL) matching the state.json name closely (minor 'Rubber'/'Rubbers' spelling variance only). Seeded 2026-09-13 via untrusted X triage (@rishithegreat41, high conviction).
fundamentals_narrative: Headline numbers are genuinely strong for a micro-cap: high ROCE/ROE, healthy revenue growth and almost no leverage. The business rides a real regulatory tailwind - India's Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) rules for waste tyres are pushing organized demand for reclaimed rubber/recycling capacity. However this is a tiny-revenue (~Rs 67 Cr) commodity-adjacent processor: reclaimed rubber is a substitute input priced off virgin-rubber/scrap spreads, with limited product differentiation. No P/E or margin detail could be confirmed in this pass, and the stock trades well off its 52-week low, so valuation comfort is unconfirmed.

quality_metrics.note: roce_pct is FY24 (most recent confirmed by screener.in; FY25/26 not disclosed there). OPM has expanded every year on record (7.79%->11.18%->14.70%->21.08% FY23-26) and ROCE improved 29.8%->37.86% - genuinely strong. But free cash flow has been NEGATIVE in all 4 disclosed fiscal years (FY23-26: -6.61, -1.78, -2.12, -3.45 Cr) even as borrowings have risen from zero to Rs 6.93 Cr - a real, previously-unflagged earnings-quality caution behind the strong margin/ROCE headline.
